[quote]Just saying, but I do have a curator page. If you like my remarks about games, you can find more of them here: https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44130985-TDP%27s-Gaming-Escapades [/quote]

One of the most interesting ideas in entertainment is crossovers, as the very idea of previously unrelated characters interacting with each other and reacting to new situations is something that is very exciting. When done properly, these crossovers become some of the most enjoyable pieces of media that you have ever consumed; But we don't always see proper care put into making them by people who were in charge.
Blade Arcus From Shining: Battle Arena is a crossover fighting game that brings characters from Shining Tears, Shining Wind, Shining Hearts and Shining Blade together for friday night fisticuffs. But in a twist, the development duties were put in the hands of Studio Saizensen, mostly known for their Umihara Kawase series and Code of Princess. Therefore, some might get very suspicious and think they are looking at nothing short of a disaster.
Well, the game is not a disaster and is actually fun to play. However, it does have some glaring problems that warrant a not recommended rating.

[h2]Not gonna lie, game is fun[/h2]
Before I begin, let me remind you that if you want to see in-depth FGC explanations and analysis, you have gotten the wrong guy. I just play a fighting game, ♥♥♥♥ around and find out, then see if my experience was fun or not. With that out of the way, let's start.
Despite Blade Arcus looking like your usual anime air-dasher, it does not play like one. Sure, the combat is very fast and there's a lot of mechanics (like assists and cancels) available to do long and intricate combos with, but there's no air dashing, most of the combat is grounded and even the simplest of attacks can wipe a HUGE chunk of the opponent's health bar in mere seconds. So, each match boils down to how you can bait the opponent to leave themselves open in order to deal massive damage, while making sure you don't do the same mistakes. As such, the game might feel a bit like Samurai Shodown, but much faster and with the addition of a whole lot of other games' mechanics to it.
The variation between the characters is also praiseworthy. Each character has a different fighting style compared to the rest of the cast, and it's pretty easy to find one or several characters you would want to play as. Therefore, the combat in Blade Arcus is very enjoyable, letting anyone and especially casuals get into it with ease.  But unfortunately, it does have two big problems. First, there are balancing issues and some characters are incredibly underpowered compared to the others. Second, there's basically no content in the game because the developers didn't bother themselves to put them in it.

[h2]YOU ARE PAYING FOR AN INFERIOR VERSION OF THE GAME[/h2]
This game has a whole lot of missing content and despite [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/446040/discussions/0/353915309340768255/#c353915309342585719]Degica Games advising the development team to implement them[/url], they just brushed it off and never did it. Why? Maybe low sales of the PC release made them think it's not worth it. But what did they expect, globally releasing a very niche fighting game with missing content and nearly zero advertisements in the first place?
The PC release is based on the v2.01 arcade build that came out before the console versions, and therefore misses all of their additional features like the art gallery, arena mode and the casual-friendly controls. Instead, the devs offered an online mode exclusively for the PC version which had problems like bad netcode and lobbies being limited to 2 players, which caused it to become vacant. To make matters worse, they released an updated version in 2019! "Blade Arcus Rebellion from Shining" is a Japan-exclusive version of the game with 2 additional characters, a new mission mode and over 200 new illustrations to unlock in the gallery.
So, by purchasing this PC release, you are getting the most barebones version of the game with absolutely no chance of getting access to the superior versions. I cannot recommend the game for this one fact alone, as it basically nukes any enjoyment you could have had with it.

[h2]It's not false advertisement... but it feels like one...[/h2]
Things get worse when we get to what the game already has. The game only has 4 modes: Story, versus, online and training. Versus requires local opponents, online is dead, and training is... well... for training. That only leaves us the story mode, which is advertised like this on the game's store pages: [b]"Explore the characters stories in an RPG style with full voice acting in Story Mode!"[/b]. Now, the full voice acting part is true and is incredibly well-done. But the rest of it?
First of all, what story exploration? What we have here is pretty insignificant and feels like an afterthought! The gist of story is that someone removes the seal on the seven soul orbs, the orbs fly out and embed themselves inside strong people, and whoever collects all of the orbs by defeating the hosts is allowed to have one of their wishes granted. So, the good guys and bad guys each make a team and move out to find the orbs and have their wish come true on the side.
That's basically Dragon Ball with a Shining theme. And contrary to what you might think, nothing of value happens in the story. The two original characters (Pairon and Ryuga) don't get a proper introduction. And as for the rest of the characters, the game assumes that you already know who they are, so it does not explain anything except for "Oh yeah, these characters know each other". Not only that, basically nothing happens when each character gets to the end. Nearly all of them either wish for nothing, or for something very trivial or dumb as a joke. Hell, even one of the characters (Sonia) does not have any storyline or ending. This is speculated to be either the devs themselves not wanting to mess with the lore of the series or SEGA not allowing it, which is pretty dumb if actually true. Crossover games are not known to have canon storylines unless explicity confirmed (e.g. Persona 4 Arena) so no one would have objected to proper endings here.
Then we have that part about exploring the stories in an RPG Style, [b]which is a complete lie.[/b] The story mode in this game is basically arcade mode with a bunch of story dialogues added in, and there's nothing in the whole game that even remotely resembles something from RPG games. I don't know why they said that, but don't go in expecting something like BlazBlue's Abyss Mode or Granblue Fantasy: Versus' RPG Mode.

[h2]Looks good, but...[/h2]
On the matter of audiovisual presentation, I personally have no issues with the game. The music tracks are well-composed, and while the character sprites (yes, those are sprites) have very limited & unnatural animations, I honestly like how they and in-turn the game looks as a whole. Taking the art and professional voice acting anto account, it seems like the devs did their best here and what they did is enough in my book. But I really cannot forgive the technical limitations.
The game barely has any graphical options. It runs in 720p resolution by default, without any way to change it, and activating the fullscreen option just maximizes the window to run in borderless mode. This means that the bigger your resolution is, the blurrier the visuals will become on fullscreen mode due to resolution mismatch, and the smaller the game's window size will be in windowed mode.


[h2]TL;DR[/h2]
The gameplay is actually really fun, but the high amount of missing content compared to console versions, the locked resolution and the dead online modes will prove to be dealbreakers.

不知道什么时候买的这个游戏大概有67年了，如果要购买只能说非常不推荐。
一.如果你非常喜欢tony老师的人设，这个游戏并没有单独鉴赏室观看立绘所以不推荐。

可能《光明》系列已经死了，想起被隔壁榨干所有价值的《北欧女神》，有时候死了走的安详也许是件好事。

[h1]Reseña de BLADE ARCUS from Shining: Battle Arena[/h1]

[h2]Resumen[/h2]
¿Te gustan los juegos de lucha con un toque de anime Japonés y personajes que parecen sacados directamente de un episodio de \Demasiado Kawaii para Luchar\? Pues, BLADE ARCUS from Shining: Battle Arena podría ser esa pequeña joya kawai que has estado ignorando en tu biblioteca de Steam. Con un desfile de personajes brillantemente dibujados y animados, este juego pretende colocar sus cartas en la mesa del género de lucha. Claro que sí, amigos, preparados para lanzar poderes y combos como si no hubiese un mañana.

[h2]Aspectos importantes e interesantes[/h2]
Lo que realmente destaca es el arte. Esos diseños de personajes son algo por lo que tirarías tus yenes al monitor sin pensar. Animaciones fluidas, golpes que sientes hasta en el alma y una mecánica de juego que es accesible tanto para novatos como para esos veteranos enarcados en las esquinas oscuras de las salas arcade. Además, la opción de combate en equipo te permite realizar estrategias conjuntas, elevando la competitividad a otro nivel.

[h2]Aspectos por mejorar[/h2]
No todo es un campo de cerezos en flor. La historia parece que la escribió un adolescente durante su clase de matemáticas, con giros tan predecibles que podrías ir a hacer palomitas en medio de un diálogo y no perderte de nada. La diversidad de personajes también sufre, porque fuera de diferencias estéticas, muchos se sienten de lo mismo.

[h3]系统和角色[/h3]
· 首先是[b]移动[/b]，传统2D格斗那种最基本的，加一个大跳（但是并跳不出来）。
· [b]关于按键[/b]：四键ABC轻中重以及一个援护键D
· 系统像其它评测说的那样，非常贫瘠。游戏有自带文字版的“说明书”教程
· 我简单说说，方便懒得去看的，以及补充说明书里没有的
A+B是投，可前后投；可长按攻击键受身，游戏没有硬倒地；游戏没有空中受身；游戏有一定程度的跃顶保护（既正逆向难以分辨的时候，拉前后任意都可以防御）
[b]关于资源[/b]
［1］生命值下面有个小小的AP槽，主要是两个作用：B+C盾防，可无视上中下段弹开对手(注意弹开后双方依然五五开)，消耗50%；6B+C，带霸体可击飞对手，可长按使对手弹墙，之后有一次dash cancel，类似EXAMU系格斗的E键，消耗0~100%
［2］支援也有个单独的槽，4格满，援护攻击可消耗1~3格，取决于你按D时的状态（立回 1格，普通技连段或压制 2格，用必杀技时 3格，被打时，3格，开大时，4格），可以通过D+A/B/C的组合键强制指定援护攻击的消耗量；
［3］支援槽下面就是常规的气槽，最大3格：A+C类似其它格斗游戏的Roman Cancel，取消你当前的普通技或必杀技硬直并继续连段，被防大不利，1格；后+A+C是后撤跳（有无敌），可以取消普通技和必杀技，1格；EX技(相应的必杀技指令B+C同按)，0.5格；大招（一般是236236C和214214C），1格
[b]关于取消和连段系统[/b]
地面上普通技可以最基本的轻中重取消，空中的连段有SMP(same move proration/prevention)，既同样的招式（注意236A和236B算不同的招式）打中第二次会直接强制中断连段受身；伤害补正计算方式很原始，就是根据hit数，此外没有任何其它的硬直，重力，击退补正，而且基本的单下攻击伤害已经挺高，如果能打出长连段伤害会很爆炸；

[h3]内容和成就[/h3]
全成就只需要最简单模式1局制用全角色通关街机模式，速度快的话甚至能全成就之后退款（我2.2小时，痛失退款），此外除了最基本的训练模式，多人模式之外，就没有任何别的内容了。


[h3]简评[/h3]
[b]优点[/b]
+ Tony大神的精美人设
+ 全成就极其容易，但也很无聊
+ 有中文，包括训练模式各种选项几乎都翻译了，虽然显示方式挺难绷的但是没啥错

[b]缺点[/b]
- 内容很少，甚至没有画廊模式，这可是核心卖点。单纯以格游角度来说，也应该有。所以为什么没有？看下面：
- 本作在steam上的评测我都翻过了，没人提到这个最关键的一点：2019年登陆主机PS4和Switch的Rebellion大更新（UI翻新，5个新角色，包括剧情，自定义，连段挑战等的数个新模式，以及角色系统相关的大量修补增改）从来没在steam平台实装。这意味着你在网上能找到的绝大部分关于此游戏的资料信息（本就也没多少），在steam版都不适用！基于此，哪怕我很欣赏对自己作品很上心，4年之后还推出新版本的制作组，但很难给一个半成品的steam版打出推荐
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3392090240
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3392090497
- 对战时角色的视觉表现挺有意思，像近期玩过的另一款老格游The Rumble Fish，通过基于骨骼绑定的分部件2D精灵图来实现伪3D的动画效果，这种技术好处是可以大量减轻纯手绘工作量，但是缺点很明显就是诸如受击反馈等交互方面的动画缺乏力度感以及不自然。至于本作是也用了这个方法，还是用3D预建模再拍下关键帧转成2D，就不清楚了。不过可以明确的是游戏开发的资金和人手确实有限（最前线社到今年为止也才20个人而已）,画面观感非常廉价
- 基于上述原因，交互动画僵硬，导致挺糟糕的操作手感和打击感。格游处女作技术积累不够，可以理解
- 场景也很粗糙，且毫无新意

While I do recommend purchasing BLADE ARCUS from Shining: Battle Arena-- I would really only recommend buying it on sale, unfortunately. The price is quite high given the relatively under developed story-line, often times simple and/or janky mechanics, and lack of overall context for the player (without the other Shining games). 

The character designs and voice-acting is very well done and the characters have distinct perspectives on the events taking place, as well as dialogue that gives insight into their personalities. However, without a third person recounting of the events taking place in regards to Issac's role and the conflict, the story mode can come off as disjointed. Once getting my bearings on the over-arcing story however, I could enjoy the insight onto each of the characters desires and intentions in regards to collecting these wishes. 

There are many endearing characters and interesting connections between each individual, as shown through their brief interactions before the fights take place. Similar to the Mortal Kombat story-telling and interconnected/world-building, without the cut-scenes of course. I will note that each story-mode was often completed within 30-40 minutes and resulted in illustrations/scenes after the end credits. Given the wide variety of characters, I was able to complete the game over a few play-throughs. 

Speaking on the fighting mechanics, some of the characters are largely overpowered and unbalanced when compared to others. I played through the story mode often at a medium difficulty and some of the AI often highlighted this unbalanced dynamics. I favored some playing styles more than others, however, coming from a self-aware, chronic button-smasher-- this game had very simple game-play that can be categorized as button-smashing, as I'm sure others have noted. 

Overall, this game is likely wonderful for those within the Shining Blade and Shining Heart fanbases, but it might fall a bit flat for those who have no understanding of this world and the characters in it. As someone who enjoyed it despite not being familiar with the franchise, I think it would have highly benefited if there was more material in it besides the story mode, tutorial, and the online play (not too sure if it's outdated). 

Having bought it on sale though (9.99? I believe), the endearing characters and interesting designs made such a price worth it. The achievements are also very easy to attain and have cute profile display thumbnails, which is a plus for me personally lol. With the elements and criticisms discussed previously, I would definitely be a bit more hesitant in making this purchase at full price.

It's hard for me to recommend this game now. I'm half and half on it.  

The fighting system shows promise. With things like being able to dash cancel from most moves to extend combos, shield block and counter, and even utilizing your assists.  No silly hype comeback factors here.  The game is also fairly pickup and playable while there isn't an Easy Auto-combo mode like many games have today (Thank God).  You can still pull some pretty decent combos for quite a bit of damage.  

Characters range from boring to fairly interesting in design, story, and playstyle. A few of them feel like typical cookie cutter characters and move sets then as you explore more of the cast you start to find the actual good characters.  

I actually like the story mode cause it's not an incredibly long winded story.  It's just start the story, witty banter, fight, a little more witty banter, and more fighting.  I can understand the character motives easily and it's enough to make me curious for some characters.  I'm not too fond of the character designs as many feel rather misleading. Like a samurai dressed as a maid. And some characters are totally generic. The "I'm clearly evil and planned this oh you defeated me I guess I'll run away now." Kind.  The worst of the stories I'm debating if it's the one who no longer wished to break plates or the one who wanted the ultimate ice cream.  Other character story's were okay or enough to make me wish that I could play whatever game they're from. (I can't cause it's a Japan only.)

What's very detrimental to this game is the lack of game modes.  You have Story Mode which may as well be Arcade Mode. Versus, Training, and Online.  This is as bare bones as it gets for a fighting game unless you know of a tournament scene or have friends willing to play this with you, this game will quickly lose your interest.  At the time I've played this You might as well cross out Online Play cause the online is a ghost town.  

The graphics are okay.  I can tell that most of the focus was put towards the character portraits rather than the sprite work.  The sprite work is okay and works for the game. 

The music is decent nothing to complain about.  Nothing really stands out to me though as to say this is the theme I always I want to hear.  But it's not painful or overused either. I can listen to this game's OST with no problem.  

Overall I wouldn't recommend this maybe if you're a Shining Series fan and just want something else to tide you over.  Otherwise not worth it.  It needs a few more modes and possibly more characters.  Or improve some of the more boring characters.

[b][i]Blade Arcus[/i][/b] é um bom jogo de luta, apresentando ao menos o básico que um jogo do tipo deve ter. O [i]design[/i] dos personagens é o ponto forte, sem dúvida, tanto visualmente como funcionalmente. Entretanto, não há muitos, contando apenas com 16. A maioria deles luta com espadas, então é interessante perceber o alcance de cada arma e o momento de contra-atacar, já que algumas espadas têm um alcance e área de acerto muito grandes. Também não se pode defender no ar, então pular é algo que deve ser feito com muita cautela, principalmente contra personagens com katanas. 

As lutas possuem um bom ritmo, nem muito aceleradas nem muito lentas, sendo muito recomendável para quem nunca jogou jogos de luta ou pretende conhecer esse nicho. Também é uma boa introdução em jogos de luta por ter as mecânicas comuns que a maioria apresenta como contra ataque, acerto de confirmação, barras de energia, agarrar, movimentos comuns, especiais e de combinação, corrida, etc. 

As partidas funcionam com um sistema de duplas, onde o segundo personagem escolhido funciona como suporte e pode lutar [i]rounds[/i] (com exceção do primeiro [i]round[/i]). Também é possível uma combinação de golpes especiais com o personagem suporte, causando muito dano. 

Para jogadores habituados com jogos do gênero, recomendo jogar o modo [i]story[/i] no [i]Hard[/i] ou [i]Very Hard[/i]. 

Não há um modo tutorial, que poderia ser interessante, mas há um manual explicativo (em inglês), bem completo, explicando as mecânicas do jogo. 

Resumidamente é um jogo de luta bonito e decente.

After playing more, I started to appreciate the game, so I have edited my review.

PROS
+ Visual design of characters is pretty cool.

CONS
